title: Analyst, Asset Management
description:
What The Role Is

The Analyst, Asset Management, will serve as a member of a team responsible for the commercial management of utility-scale and distributed renewable energy projects located across the United States. Asset Management also serves as the owner’s representative, ensuring that budget control, value optimization, and risk mitigation are performed during the entire operational lifecycle of a project.

The Analyst will work closely with the other members of the team and a wide range of Clearway departments to help maximize the value of assets, ensure contractual compliance, and support growth initiatives.

This hybrid position is located in our San Diego, CA office. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications below but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

Due Diligence on New Project Investments:

  • Support project evaluations, project agreements, contract reviews, and due diligence to help make recommendations in support of acquisitions, divestitures, and/or investments in company-developed projects.

Financial & Performance Management:

  • Provide P&L analysis and economic performance for generating assets within the assigned portfolio.
  • Perform financial analyses, project evaluations, and due diligence to help make recommendations in support of plant optimization, recovery plans, revenue enhancement, and other major capital investments.
  • Analyze, track, and update budgets, forecasts, and financial models.
  • Monitor monthly performance and variance reports; investigate and address observed deviations.
  • Investigate any major plant outages and influence the resolution or minimization of outages.
  • Review gross margin performance and work with the energy management group to explain variances due to market conditions.
  • Extract generation data from external & internal sources as needed to support various reporting needs.
  • Ensure asset financial models are updated, as needed.

Commercial Management & Administration:

  • Support business administration activities and coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure compliance with key project company agreements and financing agreements.
  • Control and manage project document organization and retention.
  • Ensure general business-related licenses, permits, and regulatory requirements are successfully managed.
  • Review project company agreements to accommodate any project modifications.
  • Prepare reports and presentations for project stakeholders as required.

Project Integration

  • Support the development of information, sharing platforms, and work management systems, including populating such systems with historical records and archiving of documents.
  • Support improvements to asset management and project handover processes.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Finance, Business, Economics, or related field.
  • 0-3 years of professional experience in asset management, data analytics, business administration, project management, contract administration, project finance, or other commercial roles.
  • Ability to read, translate, and interpret complex agreements or regulations, with an understanding of legal terminology.
  • Experience researching, analyzing, and synthesizing data and reports.
  • Developed analytical, project management, and organizational skills.
  • Strong business and financial savvy with an understanding of accounting, finance, and valuation concepts.
  • An ability to perform at a high level in a matrixed organization, working in inter-departmental teams to achieve objectives.
  • Experience in manipulating and managing large amounts of structured and unstructured data. Prior experience with the use of formulas in Excel (i.e., vlookup, sumproduct, sumif, index/match, etc.) and creating reports from scratch.
  • Ability to occasionally travel to company or project locations.

What Would Be Nice

  • Experience working in the power industry is preferred.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Power BI, including DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) for data modeling, querying, and calculations. Experience with data visualization to create interactive and impactful dashboards and reports.
  • Experience with Python for data analysis tasks, alongside using Power Query or Excel for cleaning, transforming, and integrating data from various sources to prepare datasets for reporting and insights.

title: Analyst, Procurement
description:
What The Role Is

This role supports competitive sourcing and procurement execution for battery energy storage system (BESS) equipment. This role assists with RFx development and administration, bid evaluations, supplier communications, and preparation of award recommendations, while coordinating across internal stakeholders (Development, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Construction, and Operations) to advance supplier selection, contracting, and purchase order execution. The Analyst will support ongoing contract administration activities, maintaining documentation and trackers, and contributing market intelligence related to suppliers, logistics, tariffs, and policy changes that may impact project cost and schedule.

This position will report to the Senior Manager, Procurement, and can be hybrid-based in Scottsdale, AZ, or Denver, CO offices.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Support the Senior Manager, Procurement, and category leads in executing sourcing strategies and procurement activities for equipment focused primarily on BESS equipment
  • Administer competitive RFx processes for BESS equipment, including drafting RFx packages, managing Q&A, coordinating bid submissions, and maintaining bidder lists and timelines
  • Support supplier evaluation by organizing technical and commercial inputs, documenting clarifications, and helping assess risks and opportunities (commercial terms, schedule, warranty, logistics, and bankability considerations)
  • Perform bid evaluations and scenario analyses in Excel to evaluate pricing, inclusions/exclusions, assumptions, and key cost drivers; track and report cost movements throughout negotiations
  • Support negotiations by preparing redlines/issue trackers, summarizing supplier responses, and highlighting cost, schedule, and commercial risks for internal review
  • Coordinate cross-functionally to support alignment between BESS equipment agreements and related project documents, including EPC agreements, offtake agreements, interconnection, O&M/service agreements, warranties, logistics plans, and commissioning responsibilities
  • Assist with scope reviews to help identify gaps, interfaces, and owner-furnished versus contractor-furnished responsibilities for BESS equipment packages
  • Support vendor relationship management by scheduling recurring business review meetings and ad-hoc working sessions, documenting decisions and action items, tracking progress toward commercial milestones and deliverables, and recording product roadmap updates.
  • Orchestrate and lead the Procurement and Engineering organization’s technology and cost forecasting reporting by gathering and summarizing market and commercial intelligence across all owner-furnished equipment categories (including BESS, solar, and wind)
  • Orchestrate monthly reporting by coordinating within the Procurement organization to gather pricing, technology, and sourcing inputs across departments
  • Conduct periodic market intelligence, commodity, and pricing assessments and reporting impacting OFE and EPC sourcing efforts
  • Maintain sourcing workplans, bidder qualifications, and internal trackers to support timely vendor selection
  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders to compile inputs, track open items, and support the timely resolution of questions related to equipment scope, schedule, and commercial terms
  • Perform ad hoc analyses related to equipment sourcing, market intelligence analyses, or continuous improvement opportunities identified within the department
  • Support internal reviews of material changes and deviations to standard terms by preparing summaries, tracking approvals, and maintaining version control of supplier proposals and draft agreements
  • Coordinate with Engineering to gather and maintain BESS equipment specifications, technical requirements, and documentation needed for RFx packages and contracting
  • Maintain organized procurement files and correspondence to ensure documentation is complete and audit-ready
  • Support project financing diligence by coordinating inputs and responses related to BESS equipment scope, warranties, testing, and delivery schedules
  • Provide procurement team support as needed across adjacent categories, including EPC interfaces, balance-of-plant equipment, and O&M/services, while maintaining primary focus on BESS equipment sourcing and contracting
  • Assist in the development and implementation of procurement templates, tools, and processes (RFx templates, bid tabs, trackers, and playbooks), including the incorporation of continuous improvement opportunities

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in economics, finance, procurement and supply chain, engineering, or related field
  • 1-2 years of experience in procurement, sourcing, contracts administration, project development, battery storage engineering, or a related role
  • Experience supporting RFx processes, bid evaluation/levelization, or supplier management for equipment and/or construction-related scopes (energy, industrial, or infrastructure preferred)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to summarize commercial terms, track issues, and support contract reviews and negotiations
  • Ability to travel up to 10%
  • Proficient in Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), OneNote, and document control

What Would Be Nice

  • Experience with BESS equipment supply agreements and an understanding of key commercial terms (warranty, performance guarantees, liquidated damages, logistics, and commissioning/test requirements)
  • Familiarity with battery/PCS supplier landscape and drivers such as lead times, domestic content requirements, tariffs, and shipping constraints
  • Experience supporting utility-scale renewables or energy storage projects, including coordination with engineering and construction stakeholders

title: Associate, Project Development
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Director, Project Development, the Associate, Project Development is responsible for both supporting and directly managing the development of projects across the West region of the U.S. The Associate will be a key member of the regional team that is charged with the development and execution of the construction of Clearway Energy Group’s solar, wind, and storage project pipeline across California, Hawaii, and the Desert Southwest. The position will work with the Business Development, Origination, Engineering, Project Finance, and Construction teams across the full project lifecycle from origination to commissioning and all associated activities required to bring projects to successful commercial operation.

Candidates should have prior professional renewable energy project development experience with the ability across project siting, land and real estate, regulatory and environmental permitting, interconnection, transmission, and power marketing. Candidates should also have experience with engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) engagement and have been through one or more successful project financing processes. Experience working in CAISO and the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC) power and transmission markets is preferred.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Manage and support the development of complex large-scale renewable energy projects from initial project proposal and siting, through to permitting, design, interconnection, approval, contracting, financing, and handover to construction.
  • Identify, propose, and implement creative or alternative project development approaches that reduce exposure to permitting risks, optimize development schedules, or create additional project value.
  • Support or manage due diligence on development-stage projects and portfolio acquisitions, including comparison and prioritization of multiple opportunities based on common siting, permitting, interconnection, power marketing, and other project metrics.
  • Support the administration of development services agreements with local/regional development partners; manage a network of local project stakeholders (e.g., technical consultants, surveyors, land persons, etc.).
  • Collaborate with the internal Land Acquisition team to perform and/or manage third-party-led land campaigns to secure adequate site control to support generation and interconnection facilities.
  • Collaborate with the engineering team and external consultants to evaluate site layouts and constraints, technology options, schedule implications, interconnection applications, and studies.
  • Coordinate and provide input to project interconnection requests, load-flow and congestion studies, and other necessary aspects of securing project transmission.
  • Support the negotiation and diligence of critical project contracts and agreements, including PPAs, GIAs, Turbine Supply Agreements, and EPC contracts.
  • Support projects through financing diligence efforts to support obtaining cash equity, tax equity, and/or project debt commitments before the start of construction, and at term conversion.
  • Coordinate and strategize with the Origination team on the marketing of development-stage projects for new power purchase and offtake agreements, including submitting responses to Request for Proposals (RFPs).
  • Create and manage project budgets and schedules, including navigating internal project stage-gate reviews and investment decisions.
  • Help prepare and present materials describing project development opportunities to management.
  • Maintain industry relationships/contacts and current knowledge of market drivers and industry trends to facilitate proactive development posture and early-mover positioning as opportunities materialize.

What You'll Bring

  • A bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, economics, finance, environmental science, or a related field is required.
  • Understanding and ability to navigate complex permitting pathways for energy projects in the western United States.
  • Ability to travel as required to projects within the footprint of Clearway’s West Region (>25%).
  • Minimum of 2 years of applicable experience in the renewable energy industry in the U.S., with direct experience and competence in full life-cycle development of utility-scale solar and/or wind projects.
  • Experience and familiarity with all facets of land development: landowner engagement and negotiation/contracting, title resolution, subdivision, agricultural land use/water restrictions, land (ALTA) surveys, GIS, and other real estate elements as required.
  • A high level of critical thought and a drive to manage and/or support multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Experience managing project schedules and project budgets, as well as an understanding of key project value levers (commercial, financial, etc.).

What Would Be Nice

  • Advanced study in business, finance, law, environmental science, or public policy is highly preferred.
  • Experience and knowledge of governmental mandates, environmental regulations, or customer/market signals that impact or facilitate new development of renewable projects in Clearway’s West Region are preferred.
  • Battery storage experience a plus.
  • Knowledge of the CAISO and/or WECC power and transmission markets is preferred.

title: Control Center Lead
description:
What The Role Is

Clearway Energy Group is looking for a Control Center Lead to join the Real-Time Operations Team in Scottsdale, AZ. Operating out of the Clearway Energy Group RPMC (Reporting and Performance Monitoring Center), the team currently monitors and controls 10 GW of utility-scale renewable energy plants, Wind, Solar, and BESS. The Control Center Lead will support on-shift Operations Specialists in daily operations and activities and will report directly to the Manager, Real-Time Operations. This position requires working 12.5 rotating shifts, including night, weekends, and holidays, to ensure continuous operations and monitoring of the CEG utility fleet.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Provide guidance and support to the on-shift Real-Time Operations Specialists in day-to-day job activities and responsibilities
  • Manage the RCA and continuous improvement process regarding real-time operations issues, mistakes, and common practices
  • Assist in proactively monitoring real-time activity, performance, and operational status of all wind, solar, and BESS assets
  • Assist in Real-Time Operations Specialist in understanding and identifying abnormal operations or alarm conditions that arise during the shift and appropriately troubleshoot in a timely fashion
  • Perform periodic operator log reviews for accuracy and compliance
  • Perform acceptance testing on RPMC tools or applications used by the on-shift Operations Specialist
  • Support the commission activities of new projects
  • Support and assist in the onboarding process, training, and qualification activities of new operations specialists
  • Implementation of processes and procedures to assure compliance with internal controls and quality controls for customers and field personnel, and distribute the information to the real-time operations specialists.
  • Support and assist in RFIs, data requests, and other assigned duties
  • Provide constructive feedback, mentoring, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
  • Support operational efficiency by identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and helping with best practices

What You'll Bring

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in power plant operations
  • 4-year degree or relevant experience may be considered
  • NERC Reliability Coordinator Certification or able to obtain within 6 months
  • Able to demonstrate competent technical knowledge of plant and system processes and experience in operating electrical or SCADA systems
  • Able to interpret NERC, ERCOT, WECC, CAISO, PJM, and SPP regulations and requirements
  • Available for 24-hour on-call duty to meet obligations to the Operations Team as issues arise
  • Knowledge of functional system interactions and the ability to pay attention to critical elements in a complex and regulated environment
  • Ability to make financial decisions based on real-time power plant equipment analysis and contract-related cost weighting, risk versus reward
  • Ability to coordinate multiple activities and ensure safety, quality, and schedule adherence
  • Ability to take direction, identify problems, develop solutions, conduct analysis independently and in collaboration with others
  • Ability to work in difficult customer situations
  • Previous leadership or supervisory experience
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to provide constructive feedback and resolve team challenges

title: Evening Shift Wind Technician
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Wind Site Lead, the Evening Shift Wind Technician is responsible for assisting in the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electric component maintenance. The primary objective is to maintain safe, effective, efficient, and profitable wind turbine operation.

Wind Technician levels are defined below, and the ranges will be determined based on the qualifications met.

Pay Ranges by Job Level:

Wind Technician I ($45,000 - $66,000)

Wind Technician II ($52,000 - $74,000)

Wind Technician III ($63,000 - $90,000)

What You'll Be Doing

Level I

  • Follow safety procedures, observe safe working practices and maintain a safe working environment.
  • Assist in the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical component maintenance.
  • Documents all work performed, parts used and time spent using computer based service reporting procedures.
  • Assist in troubleshooting and repair of SCADA communication systems.
  • Operate and maintain a service vehicle.
  • Maintain hand tools in good working order and well organized.
  • Work a flexible on call schedule when needed. This may include weeknights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Willingness to progress as a technician and take guidance from superiors.
  • Help in all areas of site operations as directed by Site Lead and Site Manager with minimal supervision.
  • Work a flexible on call schedule when needed. This may include weeknights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Other duties as assigned within the level I scope

Level II & III (additions)

  • Troubleshoot complicated mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical problems on variable pitch, variable speed wind turbines.
  • Assist in the training and development of lower level operation and maintenance personnel.
  • Perform all mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical component maintenance, repair and replacement to correct malfunctions.

  • Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color coded wires.

title: High Voltage Technician
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Manager, the High Voltage Technician will oversee the operation, maintenance, and repair of MV & HV electrical equipment for wind energy projects. This person must possess a minimum of five years’ experience in the troubleshooting, repair and maintenance of high voltage systems at a power generating facility, or similar industrial setting.

This position will be located at our Alta site in Mojave, CA.

If you don’t meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Support high voltage maintenance and troubleshooting. Ensure compliance to national/local electrical standards and company objectives.
  • Review, assist and/or perform high voltage switching, and grounding using approved switching orders and procedures.
  • Service, troubleshoot and repair high voltage collective systems, including overhead power lines, underground cable systems, substation switching equipment, power instrumentation and transformer equipment up to 230KV.
  • Instruct, train, and assist site personnel in safe work practices. Ensure compliance with industry safe work practices by wind site employees and contractors performing Balance of Plant work activities.
  • Review specific work for site planned outages. Ensure work includes time based or condition-based maintenance. Verify the availability/accuracy of permits, LOTOs, contractors, test equipment, repair parts and tools.
  • Be onsite during planned outages to assist and supervise as needed. Follow contractor work progress. Ensure unsatisfactory test results/conditions recorded are resolved, verified and addressed before contractor demobilization and restoration of equipment.
  • Track site discrete relay calibration due dates for assigned sites. Supervise the implementation of Company procedures by contracted testing personnel. Review and file final relay test reports.
  • Ensure modifications made to site equipment are documented for future reference. Maintain test logs.
  • Review site-specific equipment manuals for maintenance and repair requirements.
  • Maintain log books, work orders, procedures, timesheets, expense reports, requisitions and other documentation as required.
  • Work alternate shift schedule on short term basis and overtime as required.

What You'll Bring

  • Must possess a high school diploma or GED
  • Five years of relevant experience is required
  • Completion of a formal apprenticeship program or equivalent combination of work experience and technical training required

    Knowledge & Skills

    • Must have an understanding of electrical power generation, distribution, and possess a thorough knowledge of MV and HV systems including overhead, underground and substation systems.
    • Must possess a good understanding of operating procedures, environmental and safety rules and regulations, and first aid procedures.
    • Must possess a valid driver’s license – Class B, or Class A preferred.

    Must be skilled in:

    • The use of a variety of electrical test equipment and hand tools
    • Interpreting and following technical instruction furnished in verbal, written, diagrammatic and schedule formats
    • Reading and interpreting electrical drawings, technical manuals, and test reports
    • Using test gauges, digital multi-meters, oscilloscopes, and specialized test equipment to test overhead, underground, and substation equipment

    Specific areas of knowledge/familiarity:

    • NFPA 70E and Arc Flash hazards
    • Proper use of PPE, grounding equipment and switching equipment
    • Underground cable fault locating and repair
    • Battery maintenance, testing and documentation
    • Protective Relay purpose, operation, fault analyzing and event reports
    • Transformer maintenance; cooling, oil sampling and DGA analysis
    • Thermography- use, training, reporting and analysis
    • MV/HV breakers and disconnect operation, maintenance and testing
    • Must successfully function as a member and/or leader of a team
    • Proficiency in operation of an aerial lift truck for line repairs desired
    • Must be able to maintain a professional and positive company image and positive relationships with owners, customers, internal contractors and external contractors.
    • Must be able to effectively communicate verbally and in writing.
    • Employee may be required to work flexible work hours.

What Would Be Nice

  • Journeyman Lineman certification or direct substation experience preferred
  • Previous experience in SAP is preferred

No visa sponsorship or any kind of sponsorship for employment authorization is available for this role, now or in the future.

title: Lead Technician
description:
What The Role Is

This position reports to the Plant Manager and has primary responsibility for the VP/Arica assets located in Desert Center, CA.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Monitor and enforce safe work practices as they relate to PV Solar plants and PV Solar BOP repairs and maintenance.
  • Primary responsibility: responsible to maintain sites availability at the highest state of operability, meeting contractual obligations, and budget
  • Manages the plant maintenance program based on best practices in the PV industry, with an emphasis on safety, planning/scheduling, and preventive/predictive maintenance.
  • Monitor and report on manufacture and third-party maintenance and repair efforts
  • Supervise/conduct/assist in trouble shooting and repairs of electrical and mechanical systems.
  • Monitors and manages the use and inventories of spare parts, maintenance supplies, equipment, tools, and reordering as necessary.
  • Inspect completed repairs and scheduled maintenance for quality assurance.
  • Maintain logs and records as required to record complete operating conditions for the facility and report and irregularities.
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements.
  • Communicates regularly with Management and all site personnel, both individually and as a group, to ensure excellent two-way communication concerning operational and maintenance issues.
  • Participate in contract negotiations with sub-contractors and other vendors for parts and services required.
  • Responsible for manuals, updates, and work instructions for site personnel and PV systems
  • Work with team members to establish goals, action plans and strategies.
  • Develop standard work procedures.
  • Work overtime and non-standard working hours – (nights) as required

What You'll Bring

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • 3 years of experience in the operation of Commercial Solar plants or 5 years of equivalent experience in instrumentation & controls, MV/HV Electrical work.
  • Qualified to perform all routine and emergency operations at an electric generation facility and HV Switchyard.
  • Experience working with plant systems and computerized maintenance management systems. (SAP).
  • Knowledge of complex analog and digital instrumentation and control systems; proper methods for troubleshooting, repairing, and adjusting instruments and control systems; proper and safe methods to clear equipment; safe use of tools; plant safety rules; reporting procedures and practices, maintenance procedures and practices; electrical and mechanical prints, and PV Solar plant terminology and nomenclature.
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain PV solar sites at high availability.
  • Proficiency in using MS Office software to include spread sheet and document applications.
  • Understanding of general workplace safety and the ability to follow safety standards as well as help the company improve upon the standards in place.
  • If you don’t meet 100% of the above qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

title: Manager, Business Development and M&A
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Director of Business Development and M&A, the role is responsible for growing the Clearway development and operating platform for utility-scale wind, solar, and energy storage projects, as well as multi-technology complexes. This includes managing the acquisition of both development and operating assets, as well as greenfielding new development projects, in support of Clearway’s profitability and strategic goals. The role requires close collaboration with internal subject matter experts, external consultants, and legal counsel.

This hybrid role will be located in our Denver, CO office. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Manage the project acquisition process: deal origination, valuation, structuring, due diligence, negotiation, and closing of project acquisitions as a key member/manager of a transaction team.
    • Coordinate with internal and external counsel to negotiate and draft definitive transaction documentation.
    • Coordinate with internal constituents and third-party consultants to perform due diligence activities.
    • Work with subject matter experts in project development, engineering, procurement, capital markets, O&M, and others to ensure conformance with underwriting guidelines, investment metrics, and forecasted cash flows. Run sensitivity analyses and generate ideas to optimize valuations and transaction structures.
    • Prepare detailed memos and presentations for senior management and the investment committee.
    • Create and manage tools to monitor market activity and track internal origination strategy to identify new growth areas and M&A targets.
  • Support ongoing origination, development, and financing activities for projects that Clearway owns.
    • Support pricing analysis and bidding strategy to originate offtake contracts for Clearway’s 30 GW+ development portfolio of utility-scale wind, solar, and energy storage projects, as well as multi-technology complexes.
    • Work with functional groups, third-party consultants, and various other stakeholders to drive projects forward and perform quantitative analyses to support development and financing judgments.
  • Craft and implement overall strategy within specific regions, identify opportunities, and work with development to allocate the development budget strategically.
  • Drive strategy and execution in emerging growth segments including non-traditional offtake, technology, and/or financing structures, as opportunities present.
    • In consultation with external and internal resources, develop market assessments, production cost models, analytical tools, and business cases for early investments in emerging growth segments.
    • Help connect the dots internally to reposition existing assets (development or operating) for opportunities in emerging growth segments.
    • Support formation and ongoing management of strategic partnerships with major equipment suppliers, operators, investors, project developers, and other value chain participants.
  • Guide strategic initiatives to improve analytical tools and inform key business activities at Clearway.
    • Assist with ongoing efforts to improve financial optimization, underwriting, deal tracking, etc.
    • Develop innovative financial and offtake structures and improve existing quantitative analysis tools.
    • Guide special projects across internal functional groups to drive value creation throughout the development, procurement, construction, and financing processes.
    • Leverage AI tools effectively in support of the aforementioned scope.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor's Degree required in finance, business administration, or economics.
  • A minimum of 4-5 years of relevant work experience at a U.S. solar, wind, or energy storage development company/Independent Power Producer in an M&A, finance, or development role with a specific focus on M&A transactions, financial modeling/valuation, project development, and energy markets. Alternatively, the candidate may bring similar and transferable experience from an investment banking firm.
  • Comfort navigating transactions, particularly negotiation of M&A transactions.
  • Excellent aptitude for analytical and financial modeling with demonstrated attention to detail. Strong quantitative skills are a must for this position. Advanced capabilities in Excel and PowerPoint are essential.
  • Ability to effectively summarize complex issues and recommend next steps, both in writing and verbally, in a compelling manner that resonates with the audience.
  • Ability to manage simultaneous projects/work streams, set priorities, and exercise sound judgment unsupervised.

title: Manager, Operations Solar & BESS Engineering
description:
What The Role Is

The Solar & BESS Engineering Manager is responsible for leading Operations Engineering support for Clearway solar photovoltaic (PV) and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) assets. This role manages day-to-day technical support, reliability improvement, root cause analysis, operational readiness, and performance optimization for solar and storage facilities across the operating fleet.

The manager provides technical leadership for solar modules, inverters, trackers, and battery energy management systems. The role also develops engineering standards, strengthens technical knowledge management, reviews new project construction and acquisitions, and mentors engineers and technical contributors to assure safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective operation.

Our Scottsdale office is the preferred location for this hybrid position. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume

What You'll Be Doing

Fleet Technical Leadership

  • Lead Operations Engineering support for Solar PV and BESS throughout the Clearway operating fleet.
  • Direct reliability improvements, corrective action development, and root cause analysis for Solar and BESS systems.
  • Oversee systems testing (Capacity, Round-Trip Efficiency, etc) to ensure plants meet offtake requirements.
  • Recommend, prioritize, and drive solutions that maximize reliability, availability, production, safety, and lifecycle value of Solar and BESS equipment.
  • Provide technical leadership for solar modules, inverters, trackers, BESS controls, and battery energy management systems.
  • Partner with O&M, Asset Management, Performance Analytics, Real-time Performance Monitoring Center, NERC/Compliance, Construction, Procurement, Warranty, Insurance, and external vendors to resolve issues and implement fleetwide lessons learned.

Engineering Standards, Programs, and Knowledge Management

  • Develop, maintain, and improve internal Solar/BESS technical specifications, operational procedures, testing and operational readiness checklists, lessons-learned, and engineering knowledge databases.
  • Establish consistent practices for solar module performance analysis, inverter issue resolution, BESS capacity test support, battery augmentation planning, equipment obsolescence reviews, and repowering evaluations.
  • Review drawings, single-line diagrams, site layouts, technical manuals, test reports, and vendor documentation to support safe and effective operations.
  • Support training programs for site personnel and internal stakeholders by translating technical findings into practical inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting, and operating guidance.

Project, Vendor, and Lifecycle Support

  • Support new project construction and acquisition integration by identifying technical risks and gaps and ensuring preparedness for turnover to operations.
  • Provide technical support for warranties, insurance claims, vendor performance discussions, equipment replacements, product issues, and corrective action plans.
  • Manage technical workstreams, cross-functional action plans, consultant scopes, and vendor deliverables related to Solar and BESS reliability, performance, and lifecycle management.
  • Assess equipment obsolescence, repowering, augmentation, retrofit, and performance-improvement opportunities for existing solar and storage plants.

People Leadership and Team Development

  • Manage, coach, and develop Solar/BESS engineering staff and technical contributors, including goal setting, prioritization, work planning, technical review, and professional development.
  • Balance urgent fleet support with longer-term reliability, standards, documentation, and improvement initiatives.
  • Promote a strong safety culture, disciplined technical decision-making, clear communication, and practical engineering solutions that support operational excellence.

What You'll Bring

  • B.S. in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, Energy Systems, Engineering Technology, or a related engineering field.
  • 7+ years of experience related to renewable energy, energy storage, power distribution, power systems, plant operations, equipment reliability, or related industry experience.
  • Prior experience leading engineers, managing technical programs, or coordinating cross-functional technical workstreams.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and implement detailed solutions to complex technical problems and to convert lessons learned into practical standards and fleet procedures.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with site teams, executives, internal stakeholders, customers, owners, contractors, consultants, OEMs, integrators, and external partners.
  • Advanced knowledge of Solar PV and BESS operation, maintenance, controls, performance, and reliability requirements.
  • Experienced understanding of electrical power generation, plant operations, maintenance practices, inverter systems, BESS controls, and hybrid ESS + PV configurations.
  • Able to read and interpret electrical drawings, technical manuals, test reports, control diagrams, communication drawings, and plant layouts.
  • Knowledgeable in real and reactive power support and load flow analysis.
  • Knowledgeable in applicable technical standards, including UL1703, UL1741, UL9540, UL9540A, NFPA 68, NFPA 69, NFPA 70, NFPA 72, and NFPA 855.
  • Must successfully function as both a technical leader and a member of a cross-functional team.
  • Must be able to maintain a professional and positive company image and constructive relationships with owners, customers, internal contractors, and external contractors.
  • Must be able to communicate clearly, prioritize effectively, and drive closure on technical issues with appropriate urgency and documentation discipline.
  • May be required to work flexible hours at times to support fleet events or urgent operational issues.
  • Position is located in Scottsdale, Arizona, where several Operations Engineers, the Real-time Performance Monitoring Center, Procurement, and Construction are prevalent.
  • Ability to travel up to 40%.

What Would Be Nice

  • Advanced degree or professional engineering credentials are preferred.
  • Working familiarity with software tools such as ETAP, PSCAD, LabVIEW, or similar platforms is a bonus.

title: Manager/Senior Manager, EPC Procurement
description:
What The Role Is

This position is open to both Manager and Senior Manager level based on relevant experience reporting to the Director, EPC Procurement.

The Manager/Senior Manager, EPC Procurement is responsible for executing Clearway’s EPC contracting across the wind, solar, and BESS development and construction portfolio. This role leads end-to-end EPC procurement and contracting from market engagement and bidder qualification through RFP development, bid evaluation/levelization, executive-ready award recommendations, and commercial negotiations. The Manager/Senior Manager will ensuring contract structures appropriately allocate cost, schedule, performance, interface, and compliance risks, building and maintaining market intelligence on contractor capacity, supply chain and tariff impacts, and geopolitical and policy factors to inform project commercial decisions and portfolio timing.

Partnering closely with Development, Engineering, Construction, Legal, Finance, and Operations & Management, the Manager/Senior Manager provides contracting leadership, governance, and stakeholder alignment from project initiation through contract execution and ongoing administration, including change management and dispute mitigation.

This is a hybrid role based in Clearway’s Houston, TX; Scottsdale, AZ; San Francisco, CA; or Denver, CO offices.

Pay Ranges by Job Level:

Manager ($110,000-$145,000)

Senior Manager ($130,000-$180,000)

What You'll Be Doing

  • Support the Director, Procurement, in achieving the team’s mission and objectives, including development and implementation of a best-in-class sourcing strategy with a focus on wind EPCs for both new-build and repower projects
  • Orchestrate competitive RFx bidding and contracting efforts for EPC contracts, in coordination with development, engineering, construction, legal, finance, and Operations & Management
  • Conduct EPC bid review and EPC Contractor performance reviews to assess contractor risks and opportunities and recommend strategies to strengthen contractor selection
  • Oversee bid levelization through Excel workbook to evaluate baseline variances and identify key cost drivers while tracking and reporting cost movements throughout negotiations
  • Effectively lead negotiations, identifying and mitigating cost and schedule risks while ensuring alignment with Clearway policies
  • Ensure that Clearway risks are mitigated through alignment across major project agreements (TSA, Service Maintenance agreement, PPA, EPC agreement, Warranty, etc.)

  • Manage the development of bidding strategies and the qualification of bidders
  • Ensure timely and frequent engagement with key cross-functional teams on all issues related to Wind EPC Contracts
  • Support and facilitate internal team resolution on material changes to agreements across both commercial and technical issues
  • Coordinate with Engineering to gather and maintain specifications, scopes of work, and standards to be followed for Clearway’s wind projects
  • Build strong relationships with internal teams and with external vendor and contractor partners
  • Support the project financing process by coordinating inputs from wind EPC contractors and cross-functional teams to address independent engineering (IE) questions
  • Assist in the identification, development, and implementation of new contract policies and processes, including the incorporation of continuous process improvements

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in economics, finance, procurement and supply chain, engineering, or related field
  • Manager: 3-5 years of relevant EPC contracting/negotiation experience, plus 2+ years of management experience (managing employees or projects)
  • Senior Manager: 6-8+ years of relevant experience, plus 4+ years of management experience (managing employees or projects)
  • Project management, contracting, and negotiation experience with large-scale wind, solar, or battery storage development projects preferred
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong understanding of contract language and negotiation
  • Ability to travel up to 10%
  • Proficient in Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), OneNote, and document control

What Would Be Nice

  • Six or more years of wind contracting experience and an in-depth understanding of EPC contracting turbine technology is desired
  • Experience in Wind, Solar, and/or BESS EPC procurement

description:
What The Role Is

The Manager/Senior Manager, EPC Procurement is responsible for executing Clearway’s EPC contracting across the wind, solar, and BESS development and construction portfolio. This role leads end-to-end EPC procurement and contracting from market engagement and bidder qualification through RFP development, bid evaluation/levelization, executive-ready award recommendations, and commercial negotiations. The Manager/Senior Manager will ensuring contract structures appropriately allocate cost, schedule, performance, interface, and compliance risks, building and maintaining market intelligence on contractor capacity, supply chain and tariff impacts, and geopolitical and policy factors to inform project commercial decisions and portfolio timing.

Pay Ranges by Job Level:

Manager ($110,000-$145,000)

Senior Manager ($130,000-$180,000)

  • Support the Director, Procurement, in achieving the team’s mission and objectives, including development and implementation of a best-in-class sourcing strategy with a focus on wind EPCs for both new-build and repower projects
  • Orchestrate competitive RFx bidding and contracting efforts for EPC contracts, in coordination with development, engineering, construction, legal, finance, and Operations & Management
  • Conduct EPC bid review and EPC Contractor performance reviews to assess contractor risks and opportunities and recommend strategies to strengthen contractor selection
  • Oversee bid levelization through Excel workbook to evaluate baseline variances and identify key cost drivers while tracking and reporting cost movements throughout negotiations

  • Interface with EPC Contractors to gather and analyze market intelligence on emerging trends, tariff impacts, and legislative or policy changes that may influence the bidding process and project schedule
  • Manage the development of bidding strategies and the qualification of bidders
  • Ensure timely and frequent engagement with key cross-functional teams on all issues related to Wind EPC Contracts
  • Support and facilitate internal team resolution on material changes to agreements across both commercial and technical issues
  • Coordinate with Engineering to gather and maintain specifications, scopes of work, and standards to be followed for Clearway’s wind projects
  • Build strong relationships with internal teams and with external vendor and contractor partners
  • Support the project financing process by coordinating inputs from wind EPC contractors and cross-functional teams to address independent engineering (IE) questions
  • Assist in the identification, development, and implementation of new contract policies and processes, including the incorporation of continuous process improvements

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in economics, finance, procurement and supply chain, engineering, or related field
  • Manager: 3-5 years of relevant EPC contracting/negotiation experience, plus 2+ years of management experience (managing employees or projects)
  • Senior Manager: 6-8+ years of relevant experience, plus 4+ years of management experience (managing employees or projects)
  • Project management, contracting, and negotiation experience with large-scale wind, solar, or battery storage development projects preferred
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong understanding of contract language and negotiation
  • Ability to travel up to 10%
  • Proficient in Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), OneNote, and document control

What Would Be Nice

  • Six or more years of wind contracting experience and an in-depth understanding of EPC contracting turbine technology is desired
  • Experience in Wind, Solar, and/or BESS EPC procurement

title: Operations Sr. Analyst
description:
What The Role Is

This position reports to the Manager, Control Center Operations, and will be located in our Scottsdale, AZ office. The Operations Analyst is instrumental in ensuring that our functions, indications, and processes around control system performance at our renewable energy facilities are best in class. Operating out of the Clearway Renewable Performance Monitoring Center, the Remote Operations team monitors and controls ~10 GW of utility-scale renewable energy and BESS facilities.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Real-Time Monitoring: Closely monitor facility voltage and real power controls for BESS, PV, and Wind assets, ensuring all systems function within prescribed operational parameters.
  • Dispatch Error Tracking: Continuously review unit control system data to identify, flag, and correct dispatch errors.
  • Troubleshooting & Issue Resolution: Rapidly respond to operational anomalies and control system issues, leveraging a deep understanding of unit controls to implement corrective measures.
  • Help determine critical monitoring points for control system design and change management to allow operators to quickly identify control system malfunctions.
  • Work closely with SCADA/Controls Engineering and Operations IT to investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve unit errors. Collaborate with IT to design, develop, and refine real-time alarm systems associated with voltage and power controls.
  • Participate in the development and enhancement of alarms for control systems, ensuring robust notification and escalation pathways for operational variances.
  • Documentation: Author and maintain detailed control procedures, ensuring clear, accurate, and up-to-date records for all facility control operations.
  • Aid in training support through the creation and revision of training materials for Operations Specialists, sharing expertise and best practices in real-time controls and dispatch operations.
  • Apply working knowledge of CAISO, PJM, and ERCOT, NERC, etc. requirements to ensure all monitored facilities meet regulatory and operational standards for energy and ancillary services dispatch.
  • Coordinate and perform control system testing for new projects and engineering design changes on existing projects.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related discipline. Relevant experience in electrical & power generation would be considered in place of education.
  • 3+ years of experience in Control Center Operations.
  • NERC Certification preferred, required within 12 months of hire if not obtained.
  • Proficiency in plant and electrical system designs, relevant software systems (generation mgt. systems, SCADA, etc.).
  • Knowledge in NERC, ERCOT, WECC, CAISO, PJM, and SPP regulations and requirements.
  • Ability to coordinate multiple activities and ensure safety, compliance, quality, and schedule adherence.
  • Ability to take direction, identify problems, analyze root cause, and develop solutions in collaboration with others.
  • Ability to work well with others during stressful situations.
  • Ability to work well in a fast-paced, team-oriented, collaborative environment that emphasizes attention to detail, meeting deadlines, and working together to achieve company-wide goals.
  • Strong interpersonal, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office products, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
  • If you don’t meet 100% of the above qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

No visa sponsorship or any kind of sponsorship for employment authorization is available for this role, now or in the future.

title: Plant Manager
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Region Manager, the Wind Site Manager is responsible for overseeing the operations at the Tuolumne Wind Farm.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Accountable for the safe and compliant operation of an CEG wind farm installation.
  • Responsible for monitoring, upkeep, and reporting of plant performance.
  • Create an annual operating plan and provide input on an annual budget.
  • Set direction and measure operational performance of staff and site contractors.
  • Primary contact for issue resolution in performance and land utilization issues.
  • Local point of contact for land owners, local authorities and state agencies regarding environmental and contractual issues involving wind farm installations.
  • Participate in contract negotiations with sub contractors and other vendors for parts and services required for wind power installations for site.
  • Possess the ability to climb and necessary skills to troubleshoot wind turbines at a high level.
  • Perform Operation and switching of high voltage equipment using approved switching orders.
  • Possess the necessary skills to service, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair substation and collection system malfunctions.
  • Coordinate efforts of the on site turbine technicians.
  • Assist in SCADA functions such as data editing, report creation, and local SCADA problem resolutions.
  • Monitor wind conditions, SCADA reports, turbine performance, maintenance schedules and staff performance on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis.
  • Ability to write, implement and train direct reports on all CEG programs and procedures.
  • Responsible to communicate site issues with all support staff (IT, Engineering Human resources, etc..) provide follow up as needed
  • Be able to respond to plant outages on a 24/7 schedule.
  • Other duties as deemed necessary by Senior Management

What You'll Bring

  • Able to safely handle and work with objects weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance and up to 100 pounds with assistance.
  • Able to report to the work site without transportation assistance.
  • Ability to climb towers unassisted up to 300 feet. Job will require standing outside the nacelle and nosecone at the top of the turbine.
  • Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color coded wires.
  • Able to safely work in a wide range of adverse climates and environments.
  • Able to travel as required.
  • Able to work safely in a confined space.
  • Able to meet requirements of CEG’s Qualified Electrical Worker program.
  • In depth knowledge of NERC standards and other utility regulatory requirements, power purchase contracts, operations management, financial reporting.
  • Demonstrated ability to supervise and maintain high value wind installations at or above projected performance levels and within budget.
  • Proficiency with operations financial management, forecasting and controls.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the technical and business facets of a wind installation.
  • High School diploma is required.
  • A 4-year degree in business, engineering, or related field is preferred.
  • 7 years in the wind industry.
  • Possess and valid driver’s license and clean driving record.
  • If you don’t meet 100% of the above qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What Would Be Nice

  • Technical training in wind plant operations is preferred.
  • OSHA training is preferred.
  • Proficiency in using project management software, MS Project preferred.

title: Pre-Construction Analyst, Solar-BESS
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Pre-Construction Director, the Pre-Construction Analyst works with the Development, Engineering, and Procurement teams during early-, middle-, and late-stage Development Projects, bringing a Construction perspective. The Pre-Con Analyst will review project studies and designs, engineering-procurement-construction schedules, Owner Furnished Equipment deliveries, construction feasibility and risk, environmental compliance, budgets, safety plans, quality plans, contract terms and exhibits, and project finance requirements. This person will represent the Construction Team until handoff to the Construction Project Manager at Full Notice to Proceed.

This position will be based in the San Francisco, Scottsdale, Denver, or San Diego office.

If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume

What You'll Be Doing

  • Early Design and Site Feasibility: Review site and early designs for feasibility and efficiency via desktop and site visits. Identify traffic patterns, access, existing topography and soils characteristics, vegetation and trees to remove, potential protected biological and cultural resources, watercourses, wetlands, neighbors, safety and security concerns, and interconnection access.
  • Schedule Analysis and Development: Review and provide input on assumed schedule timelines for RFP process, Engineering and Procurement durations, Construction, and Commissioning timelines to Guaranteed Milestones. Work with Procurement group to coordinate Owner Furnished Equipment schedule deliveries with EPC.
  • Construction Risk: Evaluate site for risks related to access to Interconnection Facilities, neighbors and context, site access and transportation, vegetation, existing structures to demolish, security and safety requirements, temporary facilities and O&M building location, water availability, geological and hydrological considerations, soil red flags, weather impacts, dust control requirements, Fire Department Requirements, and Labor requirements.
  • Project Budget Review: Provide input on Owner’s overall project budget including EPC costs, Owner’s Construction Management costs, Per Diem requirements, and cost of key risks to be incorporated into Contingency.
  • Safety Planning and Review: Review potential EPC Site-Specific Safety Plan for adherence to Clearway Energy standards. Review and negotiate safety-related terms in EPC contract and Exhibits. Relay final requirements to Clearway Safety and Construction Execution team prior to Full Notice to Proceed.
  • EPC Contract Term and Exhibit negotiation: Review, redline, and negotiate EPC Agreement Terms related to Scope of Work, Contractor Deliverable formats, Safety Requirements, Operational Spare Parts, Payment Application-Schedule of Values-Cash flow, Quality Assurance, Liquidated Damages, and Guaranteed Milestone requirements.
  • Utility Interconnection Support: Track Utility upgrade timelines to grid synchronization and ensure EPC High Voltage scope is properly coordinated. Act as Liaison to the Construction High Voltage and Commissioning Team before construction.
  • Commissioning Team coordination: Understand and review EPC Agreement Terms and Contract Exhibits around un-energized and energized testing, commissioning, and Performance Testing. Act as Liaison to Construction Commissioning Team before construction.
  • Prevailing Wage, Labor, and Apprenticeship requirements: Identify requirements for Project Labor Agreements, Prevailing Wage, and Apprenticeship programs. Ensure scope and cost are included in the EPC contract and relay requirements to the Execution team prior to Full Notice to Proceed.
  • Pre-Work Agreement Budget Management: Review and craft PWA’s with Procurement Team, review and approve monthly invoices ensuring conformance with pre-construction cash flow schedule, collect and maintain Lien Waivers for Financial Close.
  • Day-to-Day: Flexibility required to prioritize and support multiple projects simultaneously to track to EPC readiness at Financial Close. Communicate with Pre-Construction Team daily on project status towards key milestones including RFP release, EPC Contract Execution, and Full Notice to Proceed.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Provide project updates to Pre-Construction Team and upstream leadership, participate in Development Monthly Meetings, and support documents requesting capital spend approval.

What You'll Bring

  • HS Diploma or GED is required
  • Renewable Energy construction, engineering, or project management experience
  • 3-5 years of experience with Commercial or Utility Solar Energy or Battery projects.
  • Experience working for an EPC Construction Contractor, CM Consulting Firm, Engineering Firm, or Owner/Developer.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with complex internal and external teams, building consensus and driving project and corporate initiatives
  • Experience working with Utilities, Developers, Engineers, and EPC Contractors.
  • Proven experience in project development, design and engineering, and construction with a focus on renewable energy solar and battery projects.
  • Knowledge of solar and battery energy systems, development practices, and construction processes.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
  • Proficiency in project management software and tools.
  • Strong critical thinking abilities to identify critical risks and fatal flaws.
  • Effective communication skills to liaise with diverse teams and stakeholders.
  • Willingness to work onsite and travel as required.

What Would Be Nice

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or Architecture is preferred.
  • Occupational health and safety certifications are a plus.

title: Principal BESS Engineer
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Sr. Manager of BESS Engineering, the Principal Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Engineer (or Battery Energy Storage System Manager) is responsible for preliminary engineering, fire safety engineering, technical specifications, system optimization, and procurement support for stand-alone, hybrid, and co-located BESS facilities. The Principal BESS Engineer will help deliver optimized stand-alone, hybrid, and co-located BESS facilities. The Principal BESS Engineer / BESS Engineering Manager will work with project teams, external engineering teams, vendors, third parties, and consultants to drive our class-leading, multi-gigawatt, and globally competitive project pipeline to fruition.

This hybrid role will be located in one of our office locations in Scottsdale, AZ, San Diego, CA, San Francisco, CA, Houston, TX, or Denver, CO. Scottsdale is the preferred location.

What You'll Be Doing

  • BESS Platform Development
    • Update and refine EPC contractual agreements and requirements for BESS, with a focus on EPC obligations and the division of responsibilities.
    • Evaluate, track, and optimize BESS design to conform to the latest in safety, technology, regulatory, and compliance standards.
    • Quality control BESS engineering, design, product validation, EPC touchpoints, and division of responsibilities.
    • Provide BESS subject matter expertise to project teams through origination, development, design, construction, and commissioning.
    • Develop consensus on optimal BESS design and operational strategies with Clearway’s Development, Construction, and Operations organizations given a complex technical, economic, and regulatory environment.
    • Serve as the key technical point of contact with customers and build strategic relationships with energy storage equipment and service suppliers.
    • Develop and maintain tools optimizing BESS sizing, auxiliary loads, and augmentation.
  • BESS Development Engineering
    • Generate BESS system design requirements from project requirements originating in PPA, IA, and other applicable agreements.
    • Assess a range of BESS system designs based on project-specific constraints and propose optimal solutions based on technical and commercial considerations.
    • Establish hardware and software control requirements for market applications, including utility and ISO compliance requirements.
    • Review and negotiate the technical requirements and performance guarantees in offtake agreements.
    • Develop BESS CapEx, auxiliary load, and augmentation assumptions relevant for financial modeling and underwriting.
  • BESS Project Engineering & Strategic Procurement Support
    • Technically qualify new vendors and products in internal due diligence processes. Maintain and update technical specifications used in supply contracts.
    • Support Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) teams during the request for quote phase of projects in development. Support technical coordination, RFIs, and DOR between BESS supplier and EPC contractor.
    • Support permitting and fire safety compliance requirements.
    • Support project team with design review process, construction coordination, and commissioning of BESS facilities.
    • Coordinate closed-loop learning of best practices and process improvement given lessons learned.

What You'll Bring

  • 8+ years of experience in BESS engineering, integration, development, and commissioning for utility-scale BESS projects.
  • Experience in writing technical specifications, performance requirements, and technical reports. Ability to effectively write and verbally communicate technical information.
  • Knowledge of electrical standards (UL/IEEE), Fire safety codes and standards, National Electrical Code, and interconnection standards.
  • Familiarity with technical communications protocols (TCP/IP, Modbus/TCP, etc.) and a variety of controls software/hardware platforms.
  • Familiarity or experience with energy market applications and telemetry requirements.
  • Knowledge of Power Plant Controller, Energy Management Systems (EMS), Battery Management Systems (BMS), and utility communication systems, including SCADA.
  • Basic software programming skills, especially MS Excel and Python.
  • Familiarity with energy storage product safety standards, tests, and certifications such as NFPA codes and standards (855, 72, 68, 69), UL1973 and UL9540/A.
  • Proficiency in working on a small team in a fast-paced environment and ability to multitask and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Knowledge of utility equipment specifications.

What Would Be Nice

  • Master’s degree preferred.
  • Experience in utility electrical power system projects or distributed energy resource projects preferred.

Clearway will not sponsor non-immigrant visas for this position (H-1B, TN, E-3, etc.).

title: Principal BESS Engineer
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Sr. Manager of BESS Engineering, the Principal Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Engineer (or Battery Energy Storage System Manager) is responsible for preliminary engineering, fire safety engineering, technical specifications, system optimization, and procurement support for stand-alone, hybrid, and co-located BESS facilities. The Principal BESS Engineer will help deliver optimized stand-alone, hybrid, and co-located BESS facilities. The Principal BESS Engineer / BESS Engineering Manager will work with project teams, external engineering teams, vendors, third parties, and consultants to drive our class-leading, multi-gigawatt, and globally competitive project pipeline to fruition.

This hybrid role will be located in one of our office locations in Scottsdale, AZ, San Diego, CA, San Francisco, CA, Houston, TX, or Denver, CO. Scottsdale is the preferred location.

What You'll Be Doing

  • BESS Platform Development
    • Update and refine EPC contractual agreements and requirements for BESS, with a focus on EPC obligations and the division of responsibilities.
    • Evaluate, track, and optimize BESS design to conform to the latest in safety, technology, regulatory, and compliance standards.
    • Quality control BESS engineering, design, product validation, EPC touchpoints, and division of responsibilities.
    • Provide BESS subject matter expertise to project teams through origination, development, design, construction, and commissioning.
    • Develop consensus on optimal BESS design and operational strategies with Clearway’s Development, Construction, and Operations organizations given a complex technical, economic, and regulatory environment.
    • Serve as the key technical point of contact with customers and build strategic relationships with energy storage equipment and service suppliers.
    • Develop and maintain tools optimizing BESS sizing, auxiliary loads, and augmentation.
  • BESS Development Engineering
    • Generate BESS system design requirements from project requirements originating in PPA, IA, and other applicable agreements.
    • Assess a range of BESS system designs based on project-specific constraints and propose optimal solutions based on technical and commercial considerations.
    • Establish hardware and software control requirements for market applications, including utility and ISO compliance requirements.
    • Review and negotiate the technical requirements and performance guarantees in offtake agreements.
    • Develop BESS CapEx, auxiliary load, and augmentation assumptions relevant for financial modeling and underwriting.
  • BESS Project Engineering & Strategic Procurement Support
    • Technically qualify new vendors and products in internal due diligence processes. Maintain and update technical specifications used in supply contracts.
    • Support Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) teams during the request for quote phase of projects in development. Support technical coordination, RFIs, and DOR between BESS supplier and EPC contractor.
    • Support permitting and fire safety compliance requirements.
    • Support project team with design review process, construction coordination, and commissioning of BESS facilities.
    • Coordinate closed-loop learning of best practices and process improvement given lessons learned.

What You'll Bring

  • 8+ years of experience in BESS engineering, integration, development, and commissioning for utility-scale BESS projects.
  • Experience in writing technical specifications, performance requirements, and technical reports. Ability to effectively write and verbally communicate technical information.
  • Knowledge of electrical standards (UL/IEEE), Fire safety codes and standards, National Electrical Code, and interconnection standards.
  • Familiarity with technical communications protocols (TCP/IP, Modbus/TCP, etc.) and a variety of controls software/hardware platforms.
  • Familiarity or experience with energy market applications and telemetry requirements.
  • Knowledge of Power Plant Controller, Energy Management Systems (EMS), Battery Management Systems (BMS), and utility communication systems, including SCADA.
  • Basic software programming skills, especially MS Excel and Python.
  • Familiarity with energy storage product safety standards, tests, and certifications such as NFPA codes and standards (855, 72, 68, 69), UL1973 and UL9540/A.
  • Proficiency in working on a small team in a fast-paced environment and ability to multitask and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Knowledge of utility equipment specifications.

What Would Be Nice

  • Master’s degree preferred.
  • Experience in utility electrical power system projects or distributed energy resource projects preferred.

Clearway will not sponsor non-immigrant visas for this position (H-1B, TN, E-3, etc.).

description:
What The Role Is

As a key member of the West Business Development & M&A team, the Senior Analyst will support commercial strategy and investment decisions across utility-scale wind, solar, and battery storage assets. The role will combine development underwriting and PPA bidding with buy-side and sell-side M&A execution, including valuation, financial modeling, diligence, and transaction materials. This position reports directly to the Director, Business Development & M&A.

The role will be primarily focused on CAISO, Hawaii, and other West markets, while also supporting cross-region strategic M&A, including portfolio, operating, opportunistic acquisition, and asset-sale processes. This role is primarily focused on markets in California and Hawaii but will collaborate regularly with colleagues covering the broader West region.

This position is based in our Denver office; however, San Francisco-based candidates will be considered as an exception on a case-by-case basis for the right candidate.

If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Build and own financial models for renewable energy projects. Evaluate project economics, returns, and key risks, working closely with Development, Engineering, Capital Markets, and other teams. Run sensitivities and identify ways to improve project value.
  • Evaluate acquisition and sale opportunities. Build and manage acquisition models for operating projects, development assets, and portfolios, and drive valuation analyses and operating/financing sensitivities.
  • Partner alongside M&A deal leads on several core work streams for live transactions, including review of target company information, coordination of Q&A process and management of due diligence effort across internal subject matter experts and external consultants.
  • Prepare detailed memos and presentations for senior management and investment committee.
  • Support ongoing origination, development, and financing activities for projects:
    • Support pricing analysis and bidding strategy to originate offtake contracts for Clearway Energy Group’s 25GW+ development portfolio of utility wind, solar, and storage projects
    • Develop statistical analyses to quantify risk in highly structured transactions
    • Perform quantitative and qualitative analysis to work out impediments to negotiations and closings
    • Work with functional groups, third-party consultants, and various other stakeholders to drive projects forward and perform quantitative analyses to support development and financing judgements.
  • Oversee the integration of acquired projects into Clearway’s operating fleet, coordinating with relevant teams to ensure seamless transition and operation.
  • Develop and maintain internal tools and processes for tracking all active, inactive, and closed M&A deal activities.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor's Degree with a strong academic record from an undergraduate program, ideally with focus in economics, finance, or business administration.
  • 2+ years of relevant work experience, project finance, corporate finance, consulting, strategy, corporate development, renewable energy, or a related analytical field.
  • A demonstrated interest in renewable energy projects and/or electricity markets in the United States is preferred.
  • Aptitude for analytical and financial modeling with demonstrated attention to detail. Advanced capabilities in Excel, Word, and PowerPoint are essential.
  • Experience or demonstrated curiosity integrating AI tools into analytical and deal workflows.
  • Strong oral, written, and visual communication skills. Ability to summarize complex issues and identify opportunities or next steps is critical.
  • Robust organizational skills with a mindset towards pursuing simple and efficient solutions.
  • Ability to manage simultaneous projects/work streams, set priorities, and exercise judgment independently.
  • Interest in developing management skills and desire to grow personally and professionally within our organization.

What Would Be Nice

  • A track record of M&A execution, discounted cash flow analysis and other valuation methodologies is a bonus.
