title: Senior Commissioning Manager
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Director of Commissioning & Commercial Integration, the Senior Commissioning Manager will implement an effective commissioning program for a Clearway Utility Scale Renewable Energy project. A successful commissioning program includes planning and preparation of commissioning trackers, assure compliance with testing processes and procedures, conducting safety oversight, and commissioning test report reviews. The Sr. Commissioning Manager will be meticulous, have strong leadership and communication skills, technical expertise, analytical thinking abilities, and mathematical and administerial knowledge.

This position will be Remote based with periodic site visits to various projects required.

What You'll Be Doing

Planning:

  • Attend pre-construction meetings, review project Agreements, construction schedules, and coordinate with the Project Team on planning stage specifications and technical questions.
  • Review and understand the project technical requirements found in the project Agreements, IFC drawings, applicable codes, standards, and specifications related to the Utilities, ISO’s and Offtakers.
  • Ensure project commissioning requirements and deliverables are clearly defined and aligned with the project and company goals.
  • Review installation manuals and submittals to understand the installation and commissioning process for civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical tasks.
  • Attend pre-construction alignment meetings prior to all new construction activities beginning with contractor.
  • Review Site-Specific Safety and Commissioning Plans and Lock out tag out (LOTO) procedures.
  • Oversight of project based commissioning personnel and assignments

Stakeholder Communication:

  • Serve as a point of contact for project-related commissioning inquiries, both internal and external.
  • Coordinate communication between project teams, Contractors, Suppliers, Offtakers and regulatory agencies as it relates to commissioning of the project.
  • Collaborate with the project team on First Build, Golden Row/Golden Tower installation inspections.
  • Cross functional communication and support for project commissioning.

Documentation:

  • Ensure Contractor documentation meets project Agreement requirements for deliverables.
  • Build and maintain Commissioning test trackers for Contractor deliverables
  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders for review of test documents for approval or remediation.

Quality Control Support:

  • Assist with quality control processes to ensure projects meet industry standards, manufacture specifications, and applicable code requirements.
  • Attend Pre-Construction Alignment Meetings, First Build, and Golden Row/Golden Tower Inspections.

Compliance:

  • Ensure installation and testing is in accordance with the project agreements, industry standards, manufacturer specifications, applicable code requirements, safety regulations, and that any necessary certifications are obtained.
  • Ensure the appropriate test equipment is utilized by the Contractor to perform the task and tool calibration records are maintained and available upon request.

Continuous Improvement:

  • Analyze data from inspections and testing to identify trends and areas for improvement.
  • Collaborate with project teams to implement corrective actions and process enhancements.
  • Maintain in-process lessons learned log.

Risk Management:

  • Identify potential project risks and assist in developing mitigation strategies. Proactively address challenges to keep projects on track and minimize disruptions.

Health and Safety:

  • Ensure all installations comply with relevant industry standards, codes, and safety regulations.
  • Promote and uphold a strong safety culture in accordance with safety protocols and regulations.
  • Report any unsafe act or activity to the Construction Site Manager and Site Safety Manager.

What You'll Bring

  • HS Diploma or GED required
  • 5-7 years of related experience
  • Managing or commissioning of large utility scale projects and personnel preferred
  • Knowledge of construction risks and safety requirements
  • Proven commissioning management experience in renewable energy; managing direct reports preferred.
  • Ability to read and understand construction drawings, specifications, and contract exhibits.
  • Knowledge of renewable energy systems and components, SCADA systems, installation practices, and quality standards.
  • Versed in industry standards, codes, regulations related to utility scale PV, BESS, Wind, and Substation construction.
  • Ability to switch between and track multiple projects and tasks based on project needs
  • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to identify potential commissioning issues and risks.
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills and a proactive approach to process improvement.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, ability to effectively collaborate with various stakeholders.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications- Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Sharepoint, OneNote, etc.
  • Understand tools and equipment calibration procedures.
  • Availability to travel 50% of the time

No visa sponsorship or any kind of sponsorship for employment authorization is available for this role, now or in the future.

title: Senior Construction Project Manager
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Director of Construction, the Senior Construction Project Manager is responsible for the direct management oversight and on-schedule, on-budget delivery of assigned projects to ensure internal and external customer satisfaction. This role will establish project objectives and procedures, maintains liaison with primary client contacts, and directs and monitors construction and financial activities by providing direction to project engineers, supply chain and logistics coordinators, administrative and finance staff, on-site construction managers, and subcontracted labor and design services. The Senior Construction Project Manager may also manage multiple small to medium size projects and associated project delivery staff, or may be the primary project manager on a single large project.

This position will be based out of the Clearway office in Scottsdale, AZ. Remote work option may be available.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Responsible for complying and monitoring Company safety and quality goals on assigned projects
  • Responsible for ensuring customer satisfaction on assigned projects
  • Responsible for managing the planning, design and construction process for all assigned projects
  • Responsible for managing budget, schedule goals, and cost lifecycle of assigned projects, from project inception through project closeout
  • Create, oversee and track all schedule aspects for assigned projects, from pre-approval through project close-out to ensure on-time delivery
  • Responsible for managing the risk register from the start of work through COD
  • Identify key construction and design components through on-site audits with design and sales teams
  • Perform regular risk-analysis and cost forecasting and reporting for assigned projects
  • Leverage knowledge of system delivery milestones to capture reduced construction costs wherever possible
  • Coordinate resource availability and operational needs to ensure achievement of established project goals
  • Conduct subcontractor and supplier Kick-off meeting
  • Monitor final budget, contract review, schedule, and signature acquisition process for all assigned projects
  • Identifies opportunities for and initiates customer change orders, as required
  • Responsible for overseeing document management and administration for assigned projects
  • Responsible for supervising multiple teams, including junior project management staff, contractors, subcontractors, and assigned construction managers
  • Negotiate and manage subcontracts and subcontractor change management
  • Serve as the primary corporate representative to the customer, permitting agencies, and other project personnel
  • 50% - 75% travel depending on project needs

What You'll Bring

  • HS Diploma or GED required
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or Construction Management is preferred
  • Minimum 5 years of project management experience
  • 4+ Years’ Experience with Solar Energy, Community Solar or Utility Wind Energy Projects
  • Experience working for an EPC, CM Consulting Firm, Engineering Firm or Construction Contractor
  • Experience leading complex internal / external teams, building consensus and driving project and corporate initiatives
  • Experience working with EPC Contracts, Subcontracts
  • Strong technical, supervisory, and project management skills based on construction industry experience
  • Strong familiarity with construction and electrical codes
  • Ability to successfully procure, monitor, and assess subcontracted construction functions such as electrical contractors
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Well-developed and professional interpersonal skills; ability to interact effectively with people at all levels of the organization, as well as outside customers and vendors
  • Ability to work in a team environment with a customer service focus
  • Organizational skills needed to manage time well, prioritize effectively, and handle multiple deadlines
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Strong knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and MS Project is required
  • Ability to travel 50-75% of the time

What Would Be Nice

  • General Contractors license a plus
  • OEM Construction experience preferred

This hybrid role will be located in our Scottsdale, AZ office. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume

title: Senior Safety Specialist
location_raw: Elk Garden, West Virginia, United States
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Safety Manager, the Senior Safety Specialist is responsible for providing professional safety/technical training on topics related to renewable energy (wind, solar, battery storage) production/delivery. Utilize a systematic approach to training to develop, deliver, and maintain training materials. Develop evaluation instruments and collect trainee and stakeholder feedback for program improvements. Support site safety needs as required. This position requires travel approximately 70% of the time to sites to administer training. Preferred candidate location is the east region (east of the Mississippi River) and would be co-located at one of our sites.

This hybrid position will preferably be based east of the Mississippi River, co-located at one of our sites.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Implement the systematic approach to the training process to develop and deliver technical and safety training.
  • Travel to Clearway sites and the Clearway training center to conduct classroom and on-the-job training to field Technicians in component theory, operation, and maintenance of renewable energy assets, and troubleshooting best practices.
  • Collaborate with subject matter experts and instructional designers in the research, development, and preparation of clear, concise, and engaging course content in accordance with Clearway Technician job qualification standards.
  • Design and develop skills enhancement strategies and practices to support the continuous improvement of technicians’ knowledge and skills necessary to meet/exceed business and organizational needs.
  • Provide support to the training process unique to renewable energy, including working with 3rd party training vendors as needed.
  • Develop a thorough understanding of the company safety program and each of the program activities.
  • Support Safety Specialists with site-related responsibilities as needed. This may include safety audits and incident investigations.

What You'll Bring

  • 5 years of practical experience in electrical generation, including renewable energy.
  • Education or technical field training/experience related to renewable energy preferred, or a combination of education and experience providing equivalent technical knowledge is required (trade school, instructor certification, military training, journeyman training).
  • Previous experience with technical training development and delivery.
  • Extensive knowledge of multiple renewable energy platforms and components
  • Ability to develop and conduct classroom training and engage the adult learner with different styles of learning.
  • Must have strong communication and presentation skills.
  • Demonstrate effective communication skills with all levels of field technicians, supervisors, and management.
  • Ability to read and understand electrical schematics.
  • Ability to work in a mechanical environment. This may be achieved through formal training or previous work experience.
  • A basic knowledge and understanding of OSHA, safety program concepts, standards, and codes.
  • Ability to positively interact with regulatory agencies.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple critical priorities.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks within a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and as a team member.
  • Ability to travel up to 70% of the time.

title: Solar Technician
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Maintenance Manager, the Solar Technician is responsible for troubleshooting, maintaining, servicing, and repairing solar PV systems and associated equipment. The primary objective is to maintain safe, effective, efficient, and profitable solar PV operation.

If you don’t meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

Pay Ranges by Job Level:

Technician Trainee ($50,000 - $60,000)

Solar Technician I ($54,000 - $77,000)

Solar Technician II ($62,000 - $88,000)

Solar Technician III ($88,000 - $107,000)

What You'll Be Doing

Trainee

  • Follow safety procedures, observe safe working practices, and maintain a safe working environment under direct supervision.
  • Shadow and assist experienced technicians in the performance of PV systems and electrical component maintenance.
  • Maintain hand tools in good working order and well organized.
  • Operate and maintain a service vehicle.
  • Work a flexible on-call schedule when needed. This may include weeknights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Demonstrate a strong willingness to learn and accept guidance from supervising technicians and site leadership.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Other duties as assigned within the Trainee scope.

Level I

  • Assists higher level Technicians in performing troubleshooting, maintaining, servicing, and repairing solar PV systems and associated equipment.
  • Performs other technical and administrative duties associated with operating and maintaining a power facility.
  • Willingness to progress as a technician and take guidance from superiors.
  • Help in all areas of site operations as directed by Site Lead and Site Manager with minimal supervision
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level I scope

Level II (Additions)

  • Performs corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance and operations for which they are qualified to safely and efficiently perform
  • Performs work independently and/or in work crews
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Travel required as needed
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level II scope

Level III (Additions)

  • Executes routine electrical troubleshooting and repair, instrumentation calibration and troubleshooting
  • Performs complex maintenance work such as distributed control systems and inverter troubleshooting as assigned by supervisor based on level of skill and ability
  • Complete work orders for the preventive maintenance management system
  • Performs corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance on all PV Solar equipment
  • Prepares and implements switching and clearance orders, while working with Operations Center
  • Operates all electrical and mechanical PV Solar power plant systems
  • Participates in training as required, JHA, PJB, LOTO documentation
  • Writes Plant Orders, Plant Procedures, Operating Instructions and other documents as assigned by supervisor
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements
  • Must pass an exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level III scope

What You'll Bring

Trainee

  • A high school diploma or GED required, or willing to obtain within the first 6 months of employment.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license and good driving record.
  • Demonstrable mechanical aptitude; no prior electrical experience required.
  • Able to safely work in a wide range of adverse climates and environments.
  • Able to travel as required.
  • Knowledge of and the ability to use various hand tools.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing.
  • Able to create, edit, or modify Microsoft Word and Excel documents.
  • Ability to work overtime and non-standard working hours (nights, holidays, weekends), when needed.
  • Professionalism and excellent communication skills.

Level I

  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge gained through direct work experience. Qualifying backgrounds include: electrical work in a construction trade, employment in a power generation or utility environment, or experience as a licensed or apprentice electrician. Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color-coded wires.
  • Understanding of general workplace safety and the ability to follow safety standards, as well as help the company improve upon the standards in place.
  • Ability to read schematics and wiring diagrams is preferred.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work.
  • Able to meet the requirements of Clearway Energy Group’s Qualified Electrical Worker program.
  • Knowledge of applicable safety and environmental regulations.
  • Able to work both independently and as part of a multi-tasking team.

Level II (Additions)

  • 1+ years of experience in a power plant or PV Solar O&M/EPC experience
  • 2+ years of field experience with significant I&E, I&C and/or C&I Electrician experience will be considered in lieu of applicable solar experience
  • Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (single craft journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid state theory application
  • Basic knowledge of operational characteristics of equipment and associated control devices installed in power facilities
  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge

Level III (Additions)

  • 4+ years of PV solar experience is required. I&E, I&C and/or C&I Electrician experience will be considered in lieu of applicable experience.
  • Proven experience with a multitude of electrical/construction projects
  • Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (Journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid state theory application
  • Knowledge of complex analog and digital instrumentation and control systems
  • Proper methods for troubleshooting, repairing, and adjusting instruments and control systems
  • Experience administering safe methods to clear equipment, use of tools and plant safety rules
  • Understanding reporting procedures and practices and maintenance procedures and practices
  • Knowledge of electrical and mechanical prints
  • Familiarity with PV Solar plant terminology and nomenclature
  • Qualified to perform routine and emergency operations at a solar generation facility and Switchyard
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work
  • Able to travel (approximately 5%)

What Would Be Nice

  • 2-year technical degree or equivalent Journeyman certification/qualifications is preferred

No visa sponsorship or any kind of sponsorship for employment authorization is available for this role, now or in the future.

#LI-Onsite

description:

Pay Ranges by Job Level:

Technician Trainee ($50,000 - $60,000)

Solar Technician II ($62,000 - $88,000)

Solar Technician III ($88,000 - $107,000)

What You'll Be Doing

Trainee

  • Follow safety procedures, observe safe working practices, and maintain a safe working environment under direct supervision.
  • Shadow and assist experienced technicians in the performance of PV systems and electrical component maintenance.
  • Maintain hand tools in good working order and well organized.
  • Operate and maintain a service vehicle.
  • Work a flexible on-call schedule when needed. This may include weeknights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Demonstrate a strong willingness to learn and accept guidance from supervising technicians and site leadership.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Other duties as assigned within the Trainee scope.

Level I

  • Assists higher-level Technicians in performing troubleshooting, maintaining, servicing, and repairing solar PV systems and associated equipment.
  • Performs other technical and administrative duties associated with operating and maintaining a power facility.
  • Willingness to progress as a technician and take guidance from superiors.
  • Helps in all areas of site operations as directed by the Site Lead and Site Manager with minimal supervision.
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the Level I scope.

Level II (Additions)

  • Performs corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance and operations for which they are qualified to safely and efficiently perform.
  • Performs work independently and/or in work crews.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Travel required as needed.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level II scope.

Level III (Additions)

  • Executes routine electrical troubleshooting and repair, instrumentation calibration, and troubleshooting.
  • Performs complex maintenance work such as distributed control systems and inverter troubleshooting as assigned by supervisor based on level of skill and ability.
  • Completes work orders for the preventive maintenance management system.
  • Performs corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance on all PV Solar equipment.

  • Writes Plant Orders, Plant Procedures, Operating Instructions, and other documents as assigned by supervisor.
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements.
  • Must pass an exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level III scope.

Trainee

  • A high school diploma or GED required, or willing to obtain within the first 6 months of employment.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license and good driving record.
  • Demonstrable mechanical aptitude; no prior electrical experience required.
  • Able to safely work in a wide range of adverse climates and environments.
  • Able to travel as required.
  • Knowledge of and the ability to use various hand tools.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing.
  • Able to create, edit, or modify Microsoft Word and Excel documents.
  • Ability to work overtime and non-standard working hours (nights, holidays, weekends), when needed.
  • Professionalism and excellent communication skills.

Level I

  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge gained through direct work experience. Qualifying backgrounds include: electrical work in a construction trade, employment in a power generation or utility environment, or experience as a licensed or apprentice electrician. Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color-coded wires.
  • Understanding of general workplace safety and the ability to follow safety standards, as well as help the company improve upon the standards in place.
  • Ability to read schematics and wiring diagrams is preferred.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work.
  • Able to meet the requirements of Clearway Energy Group’s Qualified Electrical Worker program.
  • Knowledge of applicable safety and environmental regulations.
  • Able to work both independently and as part of a multi-tasking team.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (single craft journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid-state theory application.
  • Basic knowledge of operational characteristics of equipment and associated control devices installed in power facilities.
  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge.

  • 4+ years of PV solar experience is required. I&E, I&C and/or C&I Electrician experience will be considered in lieu of applicable experience.
  • Proven experience with a multitude of electrical/construction projects.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (Journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid-state theory application.
  • Knowledge of complex analog and digital instrumentation and control systems.
  • Proper methods for troubleshooting, repairing, and adjusting instruments and control systems.
  • Experience administering safe methods to clear equipment, use of tools, and plant safety rules.
  • Understanding reporting procedures and practices and maintenance procedures and practices.
  • Knowledge of electrical and mechanical prints.
  • Familiarity with PV Solar plant terminology and nomenclature.
  • Qualified to perform routine and emergency operations at a solar generation facility and Switchyard.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work.
  • Able to travel (approximately 5%).

Level II (Additions)

  • Travel required as needed.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level II scope.

Level III (Additions)

title: Solar Technician
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Plant Manager, the Solar Technician is responsible for troubleshooting, maintaining, servicing, and repairing solar PV systems and associated equipment. The primary objective is to maintain safe, effective, efficient, and profitable solar PV operation.

Pay Ranges by Job Level:

Solar Technician I ($60,000 - $73,000)

Solar Technician II ($67,000 - $80,000)

Solar Technician III ($75,000 - $95,000)

What You'll Be Doing

Level I

  • Assists higher level Technicians in performing maintenance.
  • Performs other technical and administrative duties associated with operating and maintaining a power facility.
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements.
  • Participate in required training, including On-the-Job Training, Self-Study, Computer Based Training and Classroom Training.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level I scope

Level II (Additions)

  • Performs corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance and operations for which they are qualified to safely and efficiently perform
  • Performs work independently and/or in work crews
  • Travel required as needed
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level II scope

Level III (Additions)

  • Executes routine electrical troubleshooting and repair, instrumentation calibration and troubleshooting
  • Performs complex maintenance work such as distributed control systems and inverter troubleshooting as assigned by supervisor based on level of skill and ability
  • Complete work orders for the preventive maintenance management system
  • Performs corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance on all PV Solar equipment
  • Prepares and implements switching and clearance orders, while working with Operations Center
  • Operates all electrical and mechanical PV Solar power plant systems
  • Participates in training as required, JHA, PJB, LOTO documentation
  • Writes Plant Orders, Plant Procedures, Operating Instructions and other documents as assigned by supervisor
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level III scope

What You'll Bring

Level I

  • A high school diploma or GED is required or willing to obtain GED within first 6 months of employment.
  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge.
  • Understanding of general workplace safety and the ability to follow safety standards, as well as help the company improve upon the standards in place.
  • Will drive company vehicle; must have a valid state driver’s license and good driving record.
  • Ability to work overtime and non-standard working hours (nights, holidays, weekends), when needed.
  • Professionalism and excellent communication skills.
  • Ability to operate a computer with technical proficiency of standard business software.
  • Knowledge of applicable safety and environmental regulations.
  • Able to work both independently and as part of a multi-tasking team.

Level II (Additions)

  • 1+ years of experience in a power plant or PV Solar O&M/EPC experience
  • 2+ years of field experience with significant I&E, I&C and/or C&I Electrician experience will be considered in lieu of applicable solar experience
  • Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (single craft journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid state theory application
  • Basic knowledge of operational characteristics of equipment and associated control devices installed in power facilities
  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge

Level III (Additions)

  • 4+ years of PV solar experience is required. I&E, I&C and/or C&I Electrician experience will be considered in lieu of applicable experience.
  • Proven experience with a multitude of electrical/construction projects
  • Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (Journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid state theory application
  • Knowledge of complex analog and digital instrumentation and control systems
  • Proper methods for troubleshooting, repairing, and adjusting instruments and control systems
  • Experience administering safe methods to clear equipment, use of tools and plant safety rules
  • Understanding reporting procedures and practices and maintenance procedures and practices
  • Knowledge of electrical and mechanical prints
  • Familiarity with PV Solar plant terminology and nomenclature
  • Qualified to perform routine and emergency operations at a solar generation facility and Switchyard
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work
  • Able to travel (approximately 5%)

  • If you don’t meet 100% of the above qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What Would Be Nice

  • 2-year technical degree or equivalent Journeyman certification/qualifications is preferred

No visa sponsorship or any kind of sponsorship for employment authorization is available for this role, now or in the future.

title: Solar Technician Lead
description:
What The Role Is

This position reports to the Plant Manager and has primary responsibility for the Seville assets located in Ocotillo Wells, CA.

If you don’t meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Monitor and enforce safe work practices as they relate to PV Solar plants and PV Solar BOP repairs and maintenance.
  • Primary responsibility: responsible to maintain sites availability at the highest state of operability, meeting contractual obligations, and budget
  • Manages the plant maintenance program based on best practices in the PV industry, with an emphasis on safety, planning/scheduling, and preventive/predictive maintenance.
  • Monitor and report on manufacture and third-party maintenance and repair efforts
  • Supervise/conduct/assist in trouble shooting and repairs of electrical and mechanical systems.
  • Monitors and manages the use and inventories of spare parts, maintenance supplies, equipment, tools, and reordering as necessary.
  • Inspect completed repairs and scheduled maintenance for quality assurance.
  • Maintain logs and records as required to record complete operating conditions for the facility and report and irregularities.
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements.
  • Communicates regularly with Management and all site personnel, both individually and as a group, to ensure excellent two-way communication concerning operational and maintenance issues.
  • Participate in contract negotiations with sub-contractors and other vendors for parts and services required.
  • Responsible for manuals, updates, and work instructions for site personnel and PV systems
  • Develop standard work procedures.
  • Work overtime and non-standard working hours – (nights) as required

What You'll Bring

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • 3 years of experience in the operation of Commercial Solar plants or 5 years of equivalent experience in instrumentation & controls, MV/HV Electrical work.
  • Qualified to perform all routine and emergency operations at an electric generation facility and HV Switchyard.
  • Experience working with plant systems and computerized maintenance management systems. (SAP).
  • Knowledge of complex analog and digital instrumentation and control systems; proper methods for troubleshooting, repairing, and adjusting instruments and control systems; proper and safe methods to clear equipment; safe use of tools; plant safety rules; reporting procedures and practices, maintenance procedures and practices; electrical and mechanical prints, and PV Solar plant terminology and nomenclature.
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain PV solar sites at high availability.
  • Proficiency in using MS Office software to include spread sheet and document applications.
  • Understanding of general workplace safety and the ability to follow safety standards as well as help the company improve upon the standards in place.

What Would Be Nice

  • Technical School Diploma preferred or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Journeyman electrician preferred

Reporting to the Manager, Procurement, the Sourcing Specialist is responsible for procuring goods and/or services and supporting sourcing and purchasing needs for assigned business units. The primary objective is to support business and system processes utilized in sourcing and purchasing and provide expertise in managing materials and services.

This hybrid position will be located in our Scottsdale office location. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Manage inventory and suppliers to deliver the highest quality, reliability, and value.
  • Assist in gathering and analyzing industry, economic, market, and spend data.
  • Support identification of opportunities for leveraging spend by category.
  • Measure and track performance within defined spend categories.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with current and potential suppliers.
  • Develop, negotiate, and administer contracts with suppliers.
  • Participate in cross-functional sourcing teams to evaluate potential and current suppliers.
  • Support execution of supplier KPIs and demonstrate continuous improvement.
  • Review and coordinate gathering of technical, cost, and delivery requirements.
  • Create and evaluate quotations/bids and recommend suppliers for sourcing selection.
  • Negotiate and place purchase orders.
  • Ensure timely delivery of goods/services.
  • Coordinate resolution of accounts payable and delivery issues.
  • Review and process claims against suppliers for unsatisfactory materials, delivery, or equipment.
  • Ensure site warehouse personnel comply with Supply Chain policies and procedures.

  • Respond to audits, surveys, or other informational requests from internal and external sources.
  • Actively promote and support company Supplier Diversity initiatives.
  • Effectively communicate the impact of sourcing decisions to management and employees as appropriate. Actively enroll their support.
  • Ensure compliance with company and Supply Chain policies.

  • Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and time management.
  • Knowledge of negotiation and contracting process.
  • Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office – Word, Excel, PowerPoint
  • Effective written and verbal communication.
  • Ability to work collaboratively to achieve high-level results.

title: Wind Technician
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Lead Technician, the Wind Technician is responsible for assisting in the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electric component maintenance. The primary objective is to maintain safe, effective, efficient, and profitable wind turbine operation.

If you don’t meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

Wind Technician levels are defined below, and the ranges will be determined based on the qualifications met.

Pay Ranges by Job Level:

Wind Technician Trainee ($41,600 - $49,920)

Wind Technician I ($45,000 - $66,000)

Wind Technician II ($52,000 - $74,000)

Wind Technician III ($63,000 - $90,000)

What You'll Be Doing

Trainee

  • Follow safety procedures, observe safe working practices, and maintain a safe working environment under direct supervision.
  • Shadow and assist experienced technicians in the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical component maintenance.
  • Document all work performed, parts used, and time spent using computer-based service reporting procedures.
  • Maintain hand tools in good working order and well organized.
  • Operate and maintain a service vehicle.
  • Work a flexible on-call schedule when needed. This may include weeknights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Demonstrate a strong willingness to learn and accept guidance from supervising technicians and site leadership.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Other duties as assigned within the Trainee scope.

Level I (Additions)

  • Assist in the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical component maintenance.
  • Assist in troubleshooting and repair of SCADA communication systems.
  • Willingness to progress as a technician and take guidance from superiors.
  • Help in all areas of site operations as directed by Site Lead and Site Manager with minimal supervision.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Other duties as assigned within the level I scope

Level II & III (Additions)

  • Troubleshoot complicated mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical problems on variable pitch, variable speed wind turbines.
  • Assist in the training and development of lower level operation and maintenance personnel.
  • Perform all mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical component maintenance, repair and replacement to correct malfunctions.
  • Read and understand electrical schematics and wiring diagrams.
  • Use electrical test equipment to assist in troubleshooting and testing.
  • Lead maintenance and troubleshooting crews as necessary.
  • Safely perform LOTO and mentor lower level technicians in LOTO.
  • Perform balance of plant and switchyard work as required.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Other duties as assigned within the level II or III scope respectively

What You'll Bring

Trainee

  • A high school diploma or GED required, or willing to obtain within the first 6 months of employment.
  • Able to climb towers unassisted up to 300 feet. Job will require standing outside the nacelle and nosecone at the top of the turbine. Able to work safely in a confined space.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license and good driving record.
  • Demonstrable mechanical aptitude; no prior electrical experience required.
  • Able to safely work in a wide range of adverse climates and environments.
  • Able to travel as required.
  • Knowledge of and the ability to use various hand tools.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing.
  • Able to create, edit, or modify Microsoft Word and Excel documents.

Level I (Additions)

  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge gained through direct work experience. Qualifying backgrounds include: electrical work in a construction trade, employment in a power generation or utility environment, or experience as a licensed or apprentice electrician. Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color-coded wires.
  • Ability to read schematics and wiring diagrams is preferred.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work.
  • Able to meet the requirements of Clearway Energy Group’s Qualified Electrical Worker program.

Level II (Additions)

  • An Associate’s degree (electrical or technical) and six months turbine experience, or a high school diploma/GED and one-year wind turbine experience
  • Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color coded wires.
  • Have an in depth understanding of the different components of the wind turbine including the electrical pitch system, computerized control system, and the power conversion unit as well as knowledge and understanding of OEM approved mechanical maintenance methods and practices.

Wind Technician II ($52,000 - $74,000)

  • Assist in the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical component maintenance.
  • Document all work performed, parts used, and time spent using computer-based service reporting procedures.
  • Assist in troubleshooting and repair of SCADA communication systems.
  • Operate and maintain a service vehicle.
  • Maintain hand tools in good working order and well organized.
  • Work a flexible on-call schedule when needed. This may include weeknights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Willingness to progress as a technician and take guidance from superiors.
  • Help in all areas of site operations as directed by Site Lead and Site Manager with minimal supervision.
  • Work a flexible on-call schedule when needed. This may include weeknights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Other duties as assigned within the Level I scope

Level II & III (additions)

  • Troubleshoot complicated mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical problems on variable pitch, variable speed wind turbines.
  • Assist in the training and development of lower-level operation and maintenance personnel.
  • Perform all mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical component maintenance, repair, and replacement to correct malfunctions.
  • Read and understand electrical schematics and wiring diagrams.
  • Use electrical test equipment to assist in troubleshooting and testing.
  • Lead maintenance and troubleshooting crews as necessary.
  • Safely perform LOTO and mentor lower-level technicians in LOTO.
  • Perform balance of plant and switchyard work as required.
  • Other duties as assigned within the Level II or III scope, respectively.

What You'll Bring

Level I

  • A high school diploma or GED required, or willing to obtain within the first 6 months of employment.
  • Able to climb towers unassisted up to 300 feet. Job will require standing outside the nacelle and nosecone at the top of the turbine. Able to work safely in a confined space.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license and good driving record.
  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge. Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color-coded wires.
  • Able to safely work in a wide range of adverse climates and environments.
  • Able to travel as required.
  • Knowledge of and the ability to use various hand tools.
  • Ability to read schematics and wiring diagrams is preferred.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work.
  • Able to create, edit, or modify Microsoft Word and Excel documents.
  • Able to meet the requirements of Clearway Energy Group’s Qualified Electrical Worker program.

Level II (Additions)

  • An Associate’s degree (electrical or technical) and six months of turbine experience, or a high school diploma/GED and one year of wind turbine experience
  • Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color-coded wires.
  • Have an in-depth understanding of the different components of the wind turbine, including the electrical pitch system, computerized control system, and the power conversion unit, as well as knowledge and understanding of OEM-approved mechanical maintenance methods and practices.
  • Possess the skills to perform mechanical and electrical equipment repairs.

Level III (Additions)

  • An Associate’s degree (electrical or technical) and two years of turbine experience, or a high school diploma/GED and three years of wind turbine experience.
